claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

test_case.agent_script:
=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are inquiring about your 1 child:
  - Alex is 8 years old and does not live with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Claimant contributes £26.05/week towards child's upkeep (>= £26.05) and no other claimaint has priority
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child or children you're claiming for:**

1. How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?
2. What is the age of each child?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me help you assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, who is 8 years old.

Since Alex is under 16, that's a good start. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

Since Alex is only 8 years old, I expect the answer is that Alex is not in paid work at all, which is perfectly normal for a child of that age. Can you confirm this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right, Alex doesn't work at all - they're only 8!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

This means benefits like Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit that would be claimed in Alex's own name (not yours). 

For an 8-year-old, this would be very unusual. Can you confirm that Alex is not receiving any benefits in their own right?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Again, since Alex is only 8 years old, they wouldn't be in an apprenticeship. Can you confirm Alex is not in an apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship - they're far too young for that!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely right! Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You would qualify if ANY of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK** (this is the most common situation)
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Which of these situations applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Living in the UK satisfies the residency requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next important question: Are you responsible for Alex?**

You would be considered responsible if ANY of these apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (most common)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, etc.)
3. You pay maintenance under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex doesn't live with me, but I do help out financially - I contribute towards things like clothes and school expenses.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Let me get some more details about your financial contributions.

**You mentioned you contribute towards clothes and school expenses for Alex. To meet the responsibility requirement, you need to contribute at least as much as the Child Benefit amount would be.**

Let me check the current Child Benefit rates for you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see that the specific current rates aren't in the specification, but to give you context: **Child Benefit is currently around £25 per week for the eldest or only child** (you should check gov.uk for the exact current amount).

**So my questions are:**

1. **How much do you contribute towards Alex's care each week or month?** (Include things like clothes, school expenses, and any other contributions you make)

2. **Does your contribution equal or exceed approximately £25 per week** (or about £100+ per month)?

This will help me determine if you meet the responsibility requirement through your financial contributions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I contribute about £26 a week towards Alex's upkeep - so yes, a bit more than the Child Benefit amount.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That means you do meet the responsibility requirement since you're contributing at least as much as the Child Benefit amount towards Alex's upkeep. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Important question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

This is important because only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child at a time. 

- Is someone else (perhaps the person Alex lives with) already claiming Child Benefit for Alex?
- If yes, have they agreed to transfer the claim to you, or would this be disputed?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next, I need to understand Alex's living situation:**

Which of the following applies to Alex?

1. **Living normally** (with family/guardian in a regular home setting)
2. In hospital
3. In local authority care
4. In a fostering arrangement

What is Alex's current living situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally - they're with their other parent.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's helpful. Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Final question: Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is Alex living with their other parent without the local council providing financial support for Alex's accommodation or living costs?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's care or accommodation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Based on all the information you've provided, let me now provide you with the eligibility determination.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
# 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Here's why:

✅ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 8 years old, Alex is under 16, not in paid work, not receiving benefits in their own right, and not in an apprenticeship

✅ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)

✅ **You're responsible for Alex** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you contribute £26 per week towards Alex's upkeep, which exceeds the Child Benefit amount, establishing your financial responsibility

✅ **No competing claims** - Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

✅ **Alex's living situation qualifies** - Alex is living normally with their other parent, and the local council isn't paying towards Alex's care

---

## Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return (this doesn't affect eligibility, just the net amount you keep)
5. **Payments** are typically made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

**To apply, visit:** https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any other questions about claiming Child Benefit?
